item.content:encoded:
Hi! Draft is available under the "Cockroach Party" tab. It's about… um… cockroaches. And thaumaturgy. Idea was obtained from the Random SCP Concept Generator: "Cockroaches that must be fed magic."

http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/oystershell

Specific points of critique I'm looking for help with:

Is there an existing designation for individuals who can sense thaumaturgic activity?

Any suggestions for the refinement of the test logs to make them funnier or squickier or more bizarre etc

Would the article benefit from Nowak being connected to Serpent's Hand? I decided to err on the side of simplicity and left it out of this draft, but if it's a funny idea I'll add it back in.

Thanks for your time!

item.title: Nobody is Bored. (and for some reason a Hive): Re: Nobody is Bored. (and for some reason a Hive)
item.content:encoded:
First of all a big thank you also to you for taking the time and effort to give me feedback.

+ Nobody here
- Nobody still here

I believe 'gestalts' would be the correct word here?

I wanted to make a pun, as Gestalten in German can also mean "suspicious figures" in certain contexts.
As an example:

German – Einige dubiose Gestalten schlichen um das Haus herum.
English – Some dubious crooks crept around the house.

I find this funny in the context of Nobody, because Nobody is exactly the type of person who is up to something at night and in the fog.

If they're physically separated, why are they all writing on the same page?
Like it'd make sense for a few of them to get together and write on the same page but there's like…20? of them?

I had planned to make it no more than 7, but when I counted, I came up with 13 or so. I'm going to change that.

I'm a little torn on this as a whole

I see what you mean, this is also the reason why I so urgently request feedback.

If this article survives, I will certainly write a serious tale where I develop the idea of a "Nobody gang". Just the idea that they keep their personalities after the "Noodle Incident" and the whole group tries to get along with each other is very entertaining for me.

item.title: SCP draft Crit: Re: SCP draft Crit
item.content:encoded:
(Requested to take another look at this through PM)

Alright, some things are definitely better:

  • The exploration log is now written as an exploration log, which is great!
  • The Special Containment Procedures section is more structured
  • Tone has improved in the Description section
  • There are less grammatical errors and sentence structure has been improved, which makes it easier to read (however if you want to have the whole article checked for these kinds of things, you may want to find someone more knowledgeable in that field than me)

It's alright thus far, but I've noticed a very important thing: The tone in the exploration log and other documents is very unprofessional

+ Crit on tone
- Hide crit

Alright, let's take a quote:

Researcher: Have you experienced anything yet class-D? Your heart rate is slowly gaining pace.
D-45305: Yea, I'm fine. It's just… I don't want to do this anymore. Please don't make me do this, I'm very claustro-
Researcher: Hush now, you know exactly why you are here. Don't forget it. You will comply with this mission and orders and you'll not complain. Do I make myself clear?
D-45305: (Silence)
Researcher: Do I make myself clear.
D-45305: Yes. sniff
Researcher: Good rat.

If a researcher handles a D-class in this way, they can expect a lengthy disciplinary hearing from the ethics committee. Why? Because D-class are still people, even if they are used for experiments. They aren't meant to be expendable, contrary to popular belief; D-class just means that they don't have the clearance codes for almost all files and places. Calling a test-subject, even an unwilling one, ''rat'' is highly unprofessional and unexpected from a trained Foundation researcher. It should be noted that this does not apply to the d-class themselves.

Also, I've noticed that you write the researcher like some evil maniac: he's intimidating the D-class, he's saying that the D-class isn't allowed to feel happy, etc. You should understand this: The Foundation is not evil. Even if some of their decisions are questionable, they won't abuse, hurt, or destroy unnecessarily. They even have an ethics committee to ensure that this happens. Try to keep this in mind when writing the character of the researcher.

TLDR; The Foundation is not evil, but cold and calculated. Researchers don't intimidate D-class and remain professional when conducting experiments or supervising explorations.

If you're still willing to go with an assertive researcher, I have a quick example with the previous quote:

Researcher: Have you experienced anything yet class-D? Your heart rate is slowly gaining pace.
D-45305: Yea, I'm fine. It's just… I don't want to do this anymore. Please don't make me do this, I'm very claustro-
Researcher: D-45305, please continue down the tunnel. Failure to comply will increase your sentence.
(silence)
Researcher: D-45305, do you understand?
D-45305: Yes.
Researcher: Good. Please continue down the tunnel.

Something like that. Please keep this in mind when revising your exploration log.

P.S. Here's a quote, again:

Both personnel were hypnotized at the sight of SCP-XXXX-A-2 sky which represented a neubla. The sky consistently changed in color and gases creating a mesmerizing pattern to the beat of the current song playing in SCP-XXXX-A-2. It appears to have a psychological affect causing all creatures that observe it to feel relaxed and emotional.

If a property of an SCP is discovered in an exploration log, it is best to make these kinds of observations at the end of the log. You only write the things that actually happen in the exploration; it's usually based on a recording, and a recording usually doesn't tell you that someone was mesmerized or that the SCP seemed to have a special effect on them. You can make these kinds of remarks as footnotes, or as a small section after the log titled ''note'' or something like that.

That is all! (for now) If you want me to look at something specific, just DM me.

item.title: SCP-something: Man unable to communicate properly: Re: SCP-something: Man unable to communicate properly
item.content:encoded:
It's not blasphemy to ask questions! We can think of a story as a way of building up tension and stakes for the reader. The ending, in that conventional line of thinking, should be a way of relieving that tension in a way that leaves the reader. This can be a resolution of a mystery, the end of an emotional arc, or even a twist that casts the previous elements in a drastically different light.

At the moment, it seems like you're trying to relieve the tension in a bunch of different ways at once without committing to any of them. Since each of your endings are 'twists' that are mostly unconnected to each other, it seems like the article "zig-zags" between different hints without taking the time to relate them to the actual narrative. Does that make sense?
